statement: The supplied source contains no derivation of the log-odds transformation, defining it directly: for a probability $p \in (0, 1)$ with corresponding odds $\frac{p}{1-p}$, the logit (or log-odds) function is defined as the logarithm of the odds, $\operatorname{logit}(p) = \sigma^{-1}(p) = \ln\left(\frac{p}{1-p}\right) = \ln(p) - \ln(1-p) = -\ln\left(\frac{1}{p} - 1\right) = 2\operatorname{atanh}(2p-1)$, which serves as the inverse of the standard logistic function $\sigma(x) = \frac{1}{1 + e^{-x}}$.

symbols.meaning: logit or log-odds of probability p
real-valued argument to the standard logistic function
real-valued argument to the inverse-logit (logistic) function

properties.property: The inverse of the logit function is the standard logistic function: $\operatorname{logit}^{-1}(\alpha) = \operatorname{logistic}(\alpha) = \frac{1}{1+e^{-\alpha}} = \frac{e^\alpha}{e^\alpha+1} = \frac{\tanh(\alpha/2)+1}{2}$.
properties.why: The logit is defined mathematically as the inverse of the standard logistic function $\sigma(x)$.

properties.property: The logit function maps probability values from the open interval $(0, 1)$ to real numbers in $(-\infty, +\infty)$.
properties.why: As $p \to 0^+$, the log-odds approach $-\infty$, and as $p \to 1^-$, the log-odds approach $+\infty$.

properties.property: The difference between the logits of two probabilities is the logarithm of the odds ratio $R$: $\operatorname{logit}(p_1) - \operatorname{logit}(p_2) = \ln(R) = \ln\left(\frac{p_1/(1-p_1)}{p_2/(1-p_2)}ight)$.
properties.why: The logarithm of a ratio of odds expands by logarithm quotient rules into the difference of the individual logits.

properties.property: The logit function has equivalent algebraic expressions: $\operatorname{logit}(p) = \ln(p) - \ln(1-p) = -\ln\left(\frac{1}{p}-1\right) = 2\operatorname{atanh}(2p-1)$.
properties.why: Algebraic expansion of the quotient logarithm and inverse hyperbolic tangent identity.

properties.property: The Taylor series expansion of the logit function is $\operatorname{logit}(x) = 2\sum_{n=0}^\infty \frac{(2x-1)^{2n+1}}{2n+1}$.
properties.why: Series expansion of the logit function about $x = 1/2$.

properties.property: The logit function is the quantile function (inverse cumulative distribution function) of the standard logistic distribution.
properties.why: The standard logistic function is the CDF of the standard logistic distribution.

properties.property: The logit is the canonical link function for the Bernoulli distribution in generalized linear models and the natural parameter for the binomial distribution.
properties.why: It arises directly from the canonical parameterization of the exponential family for binary outcomes.

properties.property: The logit function is the negative derivative of the binary entropy function.
properties.why: Differentiating the binary entropy function with respect to probability yields $-\operatorname{logit}(p)$.

properties.property: In state estimation algorithms, log-odds probabilities can be summed instead of multiplying small floating-point numbers.
properties.why: Logarithmic transformation converts multiplication of probabilities into addition, preventing numerical underflow.

assumptions.breaks_when: $p \le 0$ or $p \ge 1$, which makes the odds non-positive or undefined due to division by zero.

assumptions.assumption: The base of the logarithm is strictly greater than 1 (standardly base $e$).
assumptions.breaks_when: The logarithm base is less than or equal to 1 or non-positive.

failure_modes.signature: Divergence to $-\infty$ or numerical `-inf` / underflow error.
failure_modes.cause: When $p = 0$, the odds evaluate to 0 and the logarithm $\ln(0)$ diverges to $-\infty$.

failure_modes.signature: Division by zero, divergence to $+\infty$, or numerical `+inf`.
failure_modes.cause: When $p = 1$, the denominator $1-p$ equals 0, causing division by zero in the odds.

failure_modes.signature: Domain error, NaN, or complex result.
failure_modes.cause: For $p < 0$ or $p > 1$, the expression $p/(1-p)$ becomes negative or ill-defined, making the real logarithm undefined.

shape: expected a derivation, produced a definition
